headline: Record backlog and higher full-year profit and EPS outlook
summary_short: Northrop's Q3 2026 sales rose 7% to $11.1B with diluted EPS of $7.89 versus $7.67; backlog hit $110B on a 1.5x book-to-bill, and 2026 guidance was raised.
summary_long: Aeronautics Systems sales rose 14% and Defense Systems 12%, while Mission and Space Systems rose 2%. Segment operating income grew 5% to $1,345M, but segment margin slipped to 12.1% from 12.3% because the prior year included a $68M favorable adjustment at Mission Systems. Total operating margin fell to 11.4% on a smaller FAS/CAS adjustment. Net awards were $16B. 2026 guidance now calls for segment operating income of $4,940-$5,040M and MTM-adjusted EPS of $29.35-$29.75.
confidence_notes: Segment operating income, segment margin, MTM-adjusted EPS and adjusted free cash flow are non-GAAP as defined by Northrop Grumman. Adjusted free cash flow includes $371M of proceeds from sale of equipment to a customer.

drivers.explanation: The CEO cites continued strong demand, record backlog and investments that provide capacity for durable growth.
Aeronautics rose on a $195M increase on F-35 from timing of material costs and sustainment volume, plus higher B-21 and B-2 sustainment sales.
Margin fell from 12.3% principally because of a prior-year $68M favorable EAC adjustment in the restricted advanced microelectronics portfolio at Mission Systems.
The effective tax rate fell to 13.4% from 16.9% principally due to higher research credits.
